title: How Much Fiber in a Baked Potato? 3.8g per Medium
description: Baked Potato: about 3.8 g of fiber per 1 medium, baked, flesh and skin (14% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in a baked potato?

answer.detail: fiber in 1 medium, baked, flesh and skin (173 g)
answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Potatoes, baked, flesh and skin, without salt

intro: Baked potato ranks #8 of 10 vegetables on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in baked potato by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in a baked potato?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists potatoes, baked, flesh and skin, without salt at 2.2 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 medium, baked, flesh and skin; 173 g) therefore has about 3.8 g of fiber and 161 calories. That is 14% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 15% of a 25 g day and 10% of a 38 g day.
White potatoes are not usually thought of as a fiber food, but a medium baked potato with the skin gives about as much fiber as a medium apple. The skin is where it is most concentrated.

sections.heading: Why the skin matters
paragraphs: USDA’s potato skin entry is about five times higher in fiber per 100 g than the flesh alone. Mashed potatoes made from peeled potatoes lose much of that.
Cooled potatoes, as in potato salad, form some resistant starch, which acts somewhat like fiber in the gut. Standard fiber figures do not count it fully.

sections.heading: How baked potato compares with other vegetables
paragraphs: Of the 10 vegetables on this site, baked potato ranks #8 for fiber per typical serving and #10 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 2.4 g of fiber per 100 calories, in the middle of the range for the foods on this site.

Close neighbors by serving: [sweet potato](/fiber-in-sweet-potato) at 3.8 g (1 medium, baked (flesh)); [green beans](/fiber-in-green-beans) at 4 g (1 cup, cooked); [Brussels sprouts](/fiber-in-brussels-sprouts) at 4.1 g (1 cup, cooked). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), baked potato is #41 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding baked potato to your day
paragraphs: Keep the skin on for baked, roasted, and smashed potatoes. Top with beans, broccoli, or chili rather than only cheese and sour cream.

Example: 1 baked potato, 1 cup broccoli, 1/2 cup black beans. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 16.4 g of fiber, with 3.8 g from the baked potato. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of baked potato?
faqs.a: 2.2 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Potatoes, baked, flesh and skin, without salt). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in baked potato (1 potato skin (only))?
faqs.a: About 4.6 g (Potatoes, baked, skin, without salt), for 58 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in potato skin?
faqs.a: USDA lists a baked skin from one potato (about 58 g) at roughly 4.6 g of fiber, more than the rest of the potato combined.

faqs.q: Are French fries a source of fiber?
faqs.a: A little, depending on portion and whether the skin is left on. Their fat and salt usually outweigh the fiber benefit.
